method: Frames: 24 of the 120 base val episodes (never trained on, the same episodes in every moka table) x 8 evenly spaced steps = 192 states; 2 noise draws per state. Every policy sees exactly the same states and the same noise.

Push: guided chunk minus base chunk (a_w - a_none) for the 5 executed steps x 7 action dims, at each policy's eval guidance w (push target 0.99 from its own contrast check, as in the evals). a_none comes from the frozen base pi0.5 and is bit-identical across all policies (checked: max difference 0).
Check: shift / noise (RMS push over RMS difference between two noise draws of the base) is 0.89-1.25 per policy, close to the 0.99 target, so the pushes are the ones the evals ran with.

Arm vs gripper: in normalised units the gripper holds 50-68% of the push energy, and the 10% largest frames hold 73-85% of it (grasp and release). Direction scores therefore use the arm (xyz + rotation, 30 numbers); the gripper and all 35 numbers are in the tooltips.

cos per frame: mean over frames of the cosine between the two pushes. cos weighted: one cosine over all frames (sum of dot products over the root of the summed squared norms), so large pushes count more. β = sum of dot products / sum of the second push's squared norm: the least-squares share of the second push inside the first.
Intervals: 95% bootstrap over the 24 episodes (frames of one episode are not independent).
cm: summed raw xyz action over the 5 steps x 0.75 cm (G0 offset calibration, open loop). Approximate; for scale only.
Baselines for 'how alike can two pushes be': two retrains on the same round-1 data (seed rows), and different chains' round 0 vs the 900 chain's round 0.
